article_title: Two decades of research on children's creativity development during primary education in relation to task characteristics
citation: O.T.A. Potters, T.J.P. van Schijndel, S. Jak, J. Voogt. (2023). Two decades of research on children's creativity development during primary education in relation to task characteristics. Educational Research Review. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.edurev.2023.100532
title: Corpus of 52 studies on creativity development in primary education analyzed descriptively and meta-analytically
description: The review's evidence base is a systematically assembled set of studies on children's creativity development in primary education in relation to task characteristics, published in the last 20 years. As the abstract states, "A total of 52 studies published in the last 20 years were systematically analyzed with a combination of descriptive analyses and meta-analyses." The corpus supported both descriptive characterization of task use and meta-analytic synthesis of developmental patterns.
requirements: Studies must concern children's creativity development during primary education and relate to task characteristics.
examples: The corpus was analyzed with descriptive analyses of task characteristics and meta-analyses of developmental patterns.
key_sources: O.T.A. Potters, T.J.P. van Schijndel, S. Jak, J. Voogt. (2023). Two decades of research on children's creativity development during primary education in relation to task characteristics. Educational Research Review. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.edurev.2023.100532

article_title: Perceived competence and related factors affecting the development of the clinical competence of nursing students at two university sites in Namibia: a cross-sectional study.
citation: Munangatire Takaedza, Jacob Victoria, Tomas Nestor. (2024). Perceived competence and related factors affecting the development of the clinical competence of nursing students at two university sites in Namibia: a cross-sectional study. BMC Medical Education, 24, 743. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-05729-z
title: 52-item researcher-developed questionnaire measuring demographic data and possible factors affecting development of clinical competence of nursing students.
description: This questionnaire was developed by the researchers based on clinical competence development literature, with educator consultation and review by three experts for face and content validity. Section A comprised five demographic questions and Section B consisted of 47 questions on learning approach, teaching approach, assessment, feedback, constructive alignment, theory–practice gap, reflection, mode of learning, resources, and teachers' competence, rated on a Likert scale from 1 = Never to 5 = Always.
requirements: pilot testing and expert review for face and content validity before deployment
constraints: self-reported measure remains relevant despite the risk of over- or underestimation of nurses' clinical competence
target_learning_goals: self-assessment of clinical competence and factors affecting its development
examples: Cronbach Alpha was 0.75 in the pilot, increased to 0.889 after actual data collection, and reached 0.924 following exploratory factor analysis
key_sources: Munangatire Takaedza, Jacob Victoria, Tomas Nestor. (2024). Perceived competence and related factors affecting the development of the clinical competence of nursing students at two university sites in Namibia: a cross-sectional study. BMC Medical Education, 24, 743. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-05729-z
